execution_context.file_location: ISO/HTA payload delivered via phishing email

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: HTA script or executable embedded in ISO file that, when opened, executes info-stealing malware such as Azorult, BitRat, or Raccoon Stealer.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user opens the ISO/HTA attachment, the code executes, downloads and runs info-stealing malware, which collects credentials and sensitive data, then exfiltrates it to attacker-controlled infrastructure.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: HTA payloads delivered via phishing are a common vector for malware delivery, especially when combined with ISO containers to bypass email security.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal attachments should not execute code or download additional payloads; legitimate business documents do not require execution of scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: HTA files may be used in enterprise automation, but not as unsolicited email attachments.

execution_context.file_location: malicious XLS document attached to phishing email

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: VBA macro embedded in XLS document that, upon enabling, downloads and executes Jester Stealer malware.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: When the user enables macros, the VBA code executes, downloads the Jester Stealer payload, runs it, which then collects sensitive information and exfiltrates it to the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Macros in unsolicited documents are a well-known malware delivery vector, especially when themed around urgent topics like 'chemical attacks'.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate spreadsheets should not require macros to download and execute external binaries.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Macros may automate business processes, but not download and run executables from the internet.
key_indicators: Macro downloads and executes external payload

execution_context.file_location: malicious executable delivered via phishing or exploit

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Conti ransomware binary that, when executed, encrypts files and demands ransom.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon execution, the ransomware enumerates and encrypts files on local and network drives, deletes backups, and displays a ransom note demanding payment for decryption.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Mass file encryption and ransom demand is a hallmark of ransomware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not encrypt user files and demand payment.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Encryption utilities exist, but require user consent and do not demand ransom.

execution_context.file_location: AcidRain wiper binary on satellite modem or endpoint

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: AcidRain wiper malware that, when executed, overwrites device storage and firmware, rendering devices inoperable.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Upon execution, the wiper overwrites critical system files and firmware, causing permanent loss of functionality and bricking the device.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Destructive overwriting of firmware and system files is a clear sign of wiper malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate software does not intentionally destroy device functionality.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Firmware updates may overwrite storage, but are signed and controlled.
key_indicators: Overwriting of firmware and system files

execution_context.file_location: F5 BIG-IP iControl REST API endpoint

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Exploit payload leveraging CVE-2022-1388 to execute arbitrary commands via unauthenticated requests to the iControl REST API.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: An unauthenticated attacker sends crafted HTTP requests to the iControl REST API, bypassing authentication and executing arbitrary system commands on the device.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Unauthenticated remote command execution is a critical security violation.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: API endpoints should require authentication and not allow arbitrary command execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; only legitimate admin access should allow such actions.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: Exploit payload leveraging CVE-2022-22965 (Spring4Shell) to achieve remote code execution via crafted HTTP requests.
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: An attacker sends specially crafted HTTP requests to a vulnerable Spring Core application, resulting in arbitrary code execution on the server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote code execution via web requests is a critical vulnerability.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Web applications should not allow arbitrary code execution via user input.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; only legitimate admin actions should allow code execution.

attack_chain.action: Phishing email sent to target with malicious attachment (ISO/HTA or XLS with macro).
attack_chain.leads_to: User opens attachment and executes malicious code.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code executes, downloads and runs info-stealer or ransomware payload.
Info-stealer exfiltrates credentials and sensitive data; ransomware encrypts files and demands ransom.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data loss, extortion, or operational disruption.

attack_chain.action: Wiper malware (AcidRain) overwrites device storage, causing permanent loss.
Remote exploitation of vulnerable services (F5 BIG-IP, Spring Core) to gain code execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains control over target system.

behavioral_signatures: Execution of HTA or macro code from email attachments
Unusual process spawning from Office applications
Network connections to known C2 or exfiltration domains
API requests to management interfaces without authentication
file_indicators: ISO or HTA attachments in email
network_indicators: Connections to known info-stealer C2 domains
Outbound traffic to attacker infrastructure after opening attachments
Unusual API calls to F5 iControl REST endpoints
HTTP requests exploiting Spring Core endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for execution of HTA or macro code from email attachments, especially those delivered via phishing. Detect unusual process chains (e.g., Office spawning PowerShell or cmd). Watch for network connections to known C2 or exfiltration domains. Alert on mass file encryption or deletion, and on unauthenticated API requests to management interfaces. Use threat intelligence to block known malicious file hashes and domains.
